bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical conflict and shipping-route disruption raising logistics costs and denting export demand — MD&A lists continued geopolitical conflicts and the prolonged situation in the Middle East and Eastern Europe as contributing to economic slowdown and uncertainty, particularly in the EU, at times reducing export demand (cited example: lower Middle Eastern off-take in the lamps business). Disruptions on key shipping routes including the Red Sea have raised freight and container costs and added supply-chain uncertainty. High inflation and relatively high interest rates in parts of the world are flagged alongside as able to slow the global economy. The Chairman/MD message confirms geopolitical conflict disrupted logistics and raised costs during the year.
- US tariff actions, protectionism and frequent trade-policy change across the Company's export markets — Risks and Concerns names uncertainty from tariffs being imposed and the continuous changes in policy and process in the USA market, with the Company estimating a minimum direct impact of around $0.5 million from announced US tariff measures while remaining watchful of further changes. Protectionist moves and tariff actions by large economies such as the USA and China are described as disrupting established trade and supply chains and creating planning uncertainty for global manufacturers. The same trend is also framed as an opportunity for the multi-locational On-Shore / Near-Shore / Off-Shore footprint, so the exposure cuts both ways.
- Restricted global supply of rare-earth materials such as Neodymium — Flagged both in the Threats list and again in Risks and Concerns as a significant risk to the industry worldwide and more specifically to the EV industry in India — relevant to the Company given its electronics, sensors and actuator products supplied onto EV platforms.
- Structural substitution of Halogen bulbs by LED in the lighting business — MD&A Threats state LED continuing to replace Halogen Bulbs remains a threat in the OE head-lamp segment. The Company retains its pole position in India in Halogen Lamps in both OEM and Aftermarket, and describes the opportunity as growing share in a dwindling market as capacities reduce worldwide — i.e. the base market itself is shrinking. Phoenix Lighting and Electricals already faced headwinds during the year, principally from lower exports to Middle Eastern markets.
- Unpredictable commodity prices and material availability squeezing cost recovery — Listed in Threats as unpredictable and unstable commodity prices and their availability, and repeated in Risks and Concerns as an ongoing concern. The Chairman/MD message notes commodity prices tested the Company's cost-recovery mechanisms across every business during the year. Management states it is ready to manage escalating commodity prices and control costs through TPM activities.
- Currency fluctuation across the multiple geographies in which the Company operates — Named in Threats and again in Risks and Concerns as an ongoing concern, reflecting subsidiaries reporting in several currencies. Mitigation described: during the year a key priority was to further strengthen the global treasury framework, foreign-exchange risk-management practices and country-specific hedging policies to mitigate the impact of currency volatility across the Group's operations.
- Labour shortages and rising labour costs in the Company's manufacturing countries — Threats specifically cite labour shortages and increasing labour costs in countries such as India, China, Mexico and Hungary — the geographies in which the consolidated cable, electronics and lighting operations sit. Service-quality and delivery issues are separately flagged as able to lead to costs and margin erosion.
- Execution risk in integrating and restructuring the acquired global businesses (SCS and the Light Duty Cable operations) — The Company completed the second tranche of the Stahlschmidt Cable Systems acquisition out of insolvency proceedings in Germany and undertook a significant restructuring of the international businesses — relocation of the Juarez facility to Matamoros, relocation of Suprajit Canada operations, warehouse relocation from Germany to Hungary, complete shutdown of the Poland plant with relocation to Morocco, toolroom relocation from Germany to Morocco, streamlining at Suprajit Jiaxing and Suprajit Lone Star, and rightsizing of Suprajit Germany. MD&A records these initiatives entailed certain expected and a few unexpected one-time costs during the year, particularly in the third quarter. Management says the turnaround is substantially complete and the Q4 EBITDA margin of the SCS entities turned positive for the first time, so the residual risk is delivery of the promised cost synergies rather than the restructuring itself.

outlook.body:
- 'De-risk and Diversify' - maintain diverse presence across geographies, products, customers and segments so the group is better placed than peers amid rising trade barriers, tariff actions and supply-chain complexity; the Directors' Report frames the same intent as 'Derisk and grow profitably' through the four divisions, STC and the upcoming brakes division.

- 'Beyond Cables' - move from component supplier to 'Technology and Solution provider' by adding subsystems and mechanisms, braking systems and electronics/mechatronics alongside cables.
- Establish braking as the next major business vertical out of the Suprajit Technology Centre, with actuators alongside it; both product lines are expected to form a significant part of revenue in coming years.
- Technology strategy centred on STC: in-house R&D and intellectual property, a centralised Technology Centre at Jigani, Bengaluru with 100+ engineers, design centres in all key manufacturing locations, and a new Technology Centre nearing completion on the land where the Company was founded in 1985 to bring engineering teams under one roof.
- Operate as a single global engineering organisation co-ordinated from India, replacing siloed regional engineering teams, to leverage cable knowledge across the group, optimise development cost and exploit time-zone advantage.
- Partner with technology players while continuing in-house development - the Blubrake ABS licensing plus strategic investment, and the Chuo collaboration which delivered a first RFQ win with the world's largest Japanese manufacturer.
- Group-wide digital transformation: phased SAP implementation across the group to standardise processes, improve data accuracy and reporting consistency and enable faster decision-making, alongside changed ERP systems at several GCM sites.
- Financial discipline: disciplined cash flow management, prudent capital allocation, effective treasury operations and rigorous working capital control, with a strengthened global treasury framework, FX risk management practices and country-specific hedging policies.
- Rename the four group divisions from Q1 of the current financial year (DCD to ICM, SCD to GCM, SED to Sensors Electronics and Displays, PLD to PLE) to refocus each on its own business dynamics, with no change to financial-disclosure grouping.
- ICM to prioritise sustained quality, effective cost management and innovative value chain practices, building on three years of Total Productive Maintenance that earned two units the JIPM Award for TPM Excellence.
- Phoenix Lighting and Electricals to rebuild aftermarket momentum, drive profitable growth and accelerate new-product commercialisation, having strengthened cost competitiveness through pricing actions and retained its EcoVadis Silver rating with an improved score.
- Grow halogen share as a 'Last Man Standing' beneficiary of reducing global halogen capacity and space vacated by larger players, while expanding into LED drop-in solutions and new aftermarket channels and categories.
- Energy and cost programmes: TPM-driven cost control, VFD/TPR machine upgrades, 1811 KW of commissioned solar at Units 5, 7 and 4, and 5.89 million units of green energy annually contracted through group captive vendors for Karnataka units.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 was a year of consolidation and footprint reorganisation rather than greenfield addition. The Company completed the second tranche of the acquisition of the business of Stahlschmidt Cable Systems (SCS) out of insolvency proceedings in Germany, and undertook a significant restructuring and reorganisation of the international businesses following the two acquisitions of LDC (Kongsberg Automotive's Light Duty Cable division) and SCS. This included relocation of the Juarez facility to Matamoros, relocation of the operations of Suprajit Canada, relocation of the warehouse from Germany to Hungary, the complete shutdown of the Poland plant with operational relocation to the Morocco plant, relocation of the toolroom from Germany to Morocco, streamlining operations at Suprajit Jiaxing and Suprajit Lone Star, and the rightsizing of Suprajit Germany. Operations across Mexico and Europe were consolidated to draw upon global reach, lower the cost base and win business worldwide; these initiatives entailed certain expected and a few unexpected one-time costs, particularly in the third quarter, but have positioned the global business for improved profitability. The main forward project is the new Suprajit Technology Centre infrastructure, expected to be operational during the third quarter of the current fiscal year, supporting new product development in braking, actuators and electronics and the upcoming braking division. Capital expenditure for the current year is expected to be approximately ₹2,000 million across the divisions. By legal entity and division the group comprises India Cables & Mechatronics with 12 plants in India, Sensors, Electronics & Displays with 1 electronics facility in India, Phoenix Lighting & Electricals with 2 DTA domestic lamp plants and 1 EOU export lamp plant in India plus Luxlite Luxembourg, and Global Cables & Mechatronics spanning Automotive (SAL) 1 EOU India, Non-Automotive 1 EOU India, Suprajit UK (including Suprajit Slovenia), Suprajit USA, Suprajit Hungary, Shanghai Lonestar China, Suprajit Canada, Suprajit Germany, Wescon-SENA (Suprajit Kansas), Suprajit Brownsville, Suprajit Matamoros, Suprajit Morocco and Suprajit Jiaxing China, alongside the Technology Center. On the energy side a 1811 KW solar plant was commissioned in Unit 5, Unit 7 and Unit 4, eliminating the need for installing higher-capacity generators, net metering agreements with TANGEDCO were completed, procurement of 5.89 million units of green energy annually through group captive power vendors was finalised and implemented for all Karnataka units as of March 2026 (with 1.2 MW under discussion for the PLE A-1 plants), and a VFD-based system installed in Units 5, 14, 12 and 16 will be extended to all other plants in a phased manner aligned with capacity expansion. Historically the group's footprint was built through seven acquisitions - five in cables and two in halogen bulbs - including Speedo Cable Business (PV) of Pricol, Phoenix Lamps Limited, Wescon Controls (Wichita, USA), CTP Gills Cables (now Suprajit Europe), Shah Concabs, the Osram Karnai plant (Phoenix Division) and the Cable Division (LDC) of Kongsberg Automotive, with new plants at SAL Bengaluru, Pathredi, Chennai, Sanand, Pantnagar, Haridwar and Manesar, a 100% EOU for non-automotive cables in Bengaluru, and the establishment of Suprajit Technology Centre, Suprajit Germany and Suprajit Canada.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects double-digit consolidated revenue growth in FY27, with consolidated EBITDA margins improving to approximately 12% to 13.5% as consolidation benefits and the turnaround of the global businesses flow through.
- The Company enters FY27 with a stronger operating base following substantial completion of global restructuring and consolidation; the Directors' Report calls the outlook satisfactory despite global uncertainties and expects good overall revenue growth.
- Restructuring of the global businesses, particularly SCS, together with the completed Mexico and Europe consolidation, offers meaningful margin-expansion headroom in the coming years.
- Cost synergy extraction across the consolidated GCM division is now the main profitability lever, with the division's future bolstered by strong wins at Shanghai Lone Star and SAL.
- Electronics (SED) is the standout growth driver - sales grew more than 25 per cent, throttle sensors gained strong market acceptance, new export contracts were secured in the United States, and the division wins contracts for electronic throttle controls, actuators, digital clusters and rotary sensors.
- India two-wheeler demand: FY 2025-26 domestic volumes touched a record of over 22 million units, up approximately 11 per cent past the pre-pandemic peak, helped by GST rationalisation, improving rural incomes and successive rate cuts; electric two-wheelers grew over 20 per cent, taking EV penetration in the segment to 6-7 per cent.
- Transition from ICE to alternative power-trains (Hybrid, CNG and EV) continues at a rapid pace in India with many emerging new players, and alternate power-trains continue to challenge the hegemony of pure-play battery electric vehicles.
- Phoenix headwinds: lower exports to Middle Eastern markets for the Trifa brand, Chinese imports and migration to retrofit LEDs in the aftermarket; SAARC markets and the OEM segment delivered strong year-on-year gains and passenger-vehicle LED supplies have resumed, though recovery is gradual.
- Opportunity from reducing global halogen bulb capacity and space vacated by bigger players to grow market share in a dwindling product range; LED replacing halogen remains a threat in the OE head-lamp segment.
- Commodity volatility pressured margins across all businesses and customer cost-recovery mechanisms remain under strain.
- US tariffs and frequent US trade-policy change create planning uncertainty and headwinds; the Company estimates a minimum direct impact of around $0.5 million from announced US tariff measures.
- Geopolitical conflict, including the war in Ukraine and Red Sea disruption, raised freight and container costs and continues to affect logistics, cost and markets, particularly in the EU.
- Restrictions on rare-earth materials such as Neodymium are flagged as a significant risk to the industry worldwide and specifically to the EV industry in India; SED responded by delivering a ferrite magnet-based solution.
- Labour shortages and rising labour costs in India, China, Mexico and Hungary, plus currency fluctuation across multiple geographies, are stated cost pressures.
- The Suprajit Chuhatsu Control Systems joint venture is assessing market entry strategies with two leading Japanese OEMs in India; one Indian plant has been approved by a key Japanese customer and business enquiries have started.
- Climatic change remains a recognised factor in the business outlook, with greater uncertainty in weather patterns across the globe.
- The Chairman states that order books show double-digit growth across segments, with strategic programmes in advanced braking and Beyond Cables products ramping up.
- The MD & Group CEO repeats that order books show double-digit growth across existing product segments, beyond which multiple strategic projects are ramping up in advanced braking systems and Beyond Cables products.
- The Directors' Report notes strong order wins in the automotive division across geographies.
- GCM reported strong new business wins with strategic progress across several key customers, significant business development with leading global electric vehicle manufacturers and growth in China.
- SED recorded impressive order wins, including smart cluster wins on a new electric superbike platform and with a major construction equipment manufacturer, and is poised to launch a switch programme for a key electric vehicle customer.
- A range of innovative products developed at STC are at an advanced stage of testing with customers.

risks.note: Risks and Concerns names uncertainty from tariffs being imposed and the continuous changes in policy and process in the USA market, with the Company estimating a minimum direct impact of around $0.5 million from announced US tariff measures while remaining watchful of further changes. Protectionist moves and tariff actions by large economies such as the USA and China are described as disrupting established trade and supply chains and creating planning uncertainty for global manufacturers. The same trend is also framed as an opportunity for the multi-locational On-Shore / Near-Shore / Off-Shore footprint, so the exposure cuts both ways.

risks.risk: Restricted global supply of rare-earth materials such as Neodymium
risks.note: Flagged both in the Threats list and again in Risks and Concerns as a significant risk to the industry worldwide and more specifically to the EV industry in India — relevant to the Company given its electronics, sensors and actuator products supplied onto EV platforms.

risks.risk: Structural substitution of Halogen bulbs by LED in the lighting business
risks.note: MD&A Threats state LED continuing to replace Halogen Bulbs remains a threat in the OE head-lamp segment. Phoenix Lighting and Electricals already faced headwinds during the year, principally from lower exports to Middle Eastern markets.

risks.risk: Unpredictable commodity prices and material availability squeezing cost recovery
risks.note: Listed in Threats as unpredictable and unstable commodity prices and their availability, and repeated in Risks and Concerns as an ongoing concern. Management states it is ready to manage escalating commodity prices and control costs through TPM activities.

risks.risk: Currency fluctuation across the multiple geographies in which the Company operates
risks.note: Named in Threats and again in Risks and Concerns as an ongoing concern, reflecting subsidiaries reporting in several currencies. Mitigation described: during the year a key priority was to further strengthen the global treasury framework, foreign-exchange risk-management practices and country-specific hedging policies to mitigate the impact of currency volatility across the Group's operations.

risks.risk: Labour shortages and rising labour costs in the Company's manufacturing countries
risks.note: Threats specifically cite labour shortages and increasing labour costs in countries such as India, China, Mexico and Hungary — the geographies in which the consolidated cable, electronics and lighting operations sit. risks.risk: Execution risk in integrating and restructuring the acquired global businesses (SCS and the Light Duty Cable operations)

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Suprajit Engineering is the world's market leader in automotive cables and the third largest manufacturer of control cables by volume, producing more than 300 million cables a year from a footprint spanning India, the United States, Mexico, Europe, China and Morocco.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and trades automotive cables and components, non-automotive cables and components, halogen lamps, LED drop-in solutions, digital and mechanical instrument clusters, mechatronic products such as seat latches, steering locks and head-rest mechanisms, and braking products including brake shoes, brake pads, combi-brake systems and brake lever assemblies. It supplies leading global and domestic OEMs, Tier-1 automotive suppliers, aftermarket distributors and industrial equipment manufacturers across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, off-highway equipment, agricultural machinery, industrial applications and specialty lighting. Management reports the group as a single business segment - the manufacturing and selling of automotive and other components - but explains performance through divisional break-downs at the product and customer level.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects double-digit consolidated revenue growth in FY27, with consolidated EBITDA margins improving to approximately 12% to 13.5% as consolidation benefits and the turnaround of the global businesses flow through.
- The Company enters FY27 with a stronger operating base following substantial completion of global restructuring and consolidation; the Directors' Report calls the outlook satisfactory despite global uncertainties and expects good overall revenue growth.
- Restructuring of the global businesses, particularly SCS, together with the completed Mexico and Europe consolidation, offers meaningful margin-expansion headroom in the coming years.
- Cost synergy extraction across the consolidated GCM division is now the main profitability lever, with the division's future bolstered by strong wins at Shanghai Lone Star and SAL.
- Electronics (SED) is the standout growth driver - sales grew more than 25 per cent, throttle sensors gained strong market acceptance, new export contracts were secured in the United States, and the division wins contracts for electronic throttle controls, actuators, digital clusters and rotary sensors.
- India two-wheeler demand: FY 2025-26 domestic volumes touched a record of over 22 million units, up approximately 11 per cent past the pre-pandemic peak, helped by GST rationalisation, improving rural incomes and successive rate cuts; electric two-wheelers grew over 20 per cent, taking EV penetration in the segment to 6-7 per cent.
- Transition from ICE to alternative power-trains (Hybrid, CNG and EV) continues at a rapid pace in India with many emerging new players, and alternate power-trains continue to challenge the hegemony of pure-play battery electric vehicles.
- Phoenix headwinds: lower exports to Middle Eastern markets for the Trifa brand, Chinese imports and migration to retrofit LEDs in the aftermarket; SAARC markets and the OEM segment delivered strong year-on-year gains and passenger-vehicle LED supplies have resumed, though recovery is gradual.
- Opportunity from reducing global halogen bulb capacity and space vacated by bigger players to grow market share in a dwindling product range; LED replacing halogen remains a threat in the OE head-lamp segment.
- Commodity volatility pressured margins across all businesses and customer cost-recovery mechanisms remain under strain.
- US tariffs and frequent US trade-policy change create planning uncertainty and headwinds; the Company estimates a minimum direct impact of around $0.5 million from announced US tariff measures.
- Geopolitical conflict, including the war in Ukraine and Red Sea disruption, raised freight and container costs and continues to affect logistics, cost and markets, particularly in the EU.
- Restrictions on rare-earth materials such as Neodymium are flagged as a significant risk to the industry worldwide and specifically to the EV industry in India; SED responded by delivering a ferrite magnet-based solution.
- Labour shortages and rising labour costs in India, China, Mexico and Hungary, plus currency fluctuation across multiple geographies, are stated cost pressures.
- The Suprajit Chuhatsu Control Systems joint venture is assessing market entry strategies with two leading Japanese OEMs in India; one Indian plant has been approved by a key Japanese customer and business enquiries have started.
- Climatic change remains a recognised factor in the business outlook, with greater uncertainty in weather patterns across the globe.
- The Chairman states that order books show double-digit growth across segments, with strategic programmes in advanced braking and Beyond Cables products ramping up.
- The MD & Group CEO repeats that order books show double-digit growth across existing product segments, beyond which multiple strategic projects are ramping up in advanced braking systems and Beyond Cables products.
- The Directors' Report notes strong order wins in the automotive division across geographies.
- GCM reported strong new business wins with strategic progress across several key customers, significant business development with leading global electric vehicle manufacturers and growth in China.
- SED recorded impressive order wins, including smart cluster wins on a new electric superbike platform and with a major construction equipment manufacturer, and is poised to launch a switch programme for a key electric vehicle customer.
- A range of innovative products developed at STC are at an advanced stage of testing with customers.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 was a year of consolidation and footprint reorganisation rather than greenfield addition. The Company completed the second tranche of the acquisition of the business of Stahlschmidt Cable Systems (SCS) out of insolvency proceedings in Germany, and undertook a significant restructuring and reorganisation of the international businesses following the two acquisitions of LDC (Kongsberg Automotive's Light Duty Cable division) and SCS. This included relocation of the Juarez facility to Matamoros, relocation of the operations of Suprajit Canada, relocation of the warehouse from Germany to Hungary, the complete shutdown of the Poland plant with operational relocation to the Morocco plant, relocation of the toolroom from Germany to Morocco, streamlining operations at Suprajit Jiaxing and Suprajit Lone Star, and the rightsizing of Suprajit Germany. Operations across Mexico and Europe were consolidated to draw upon global reach, lower the cost base and win business worldwide; these initiatives entailed certain expected and a few unexpected one-time costs, particularly in the third quarter, but have positioned the global business for improved profitability. The main forward project is the new Suprajit Technology Centre infrastructure, expected to be operational during the third quarter of the current fiscal year, supporting new product development in braking, actuators and electronics and the upcoming braking division. Capital expenditure for the current year is expected to be approximately ₹2,000 million across the divisions. By legal entity and division the group comprises India Cables & Mechatronics with 12 plants in India, Sensors, Electronics & Displays with 1 electronics facility in India, Phoenix Lighting & Electricals with 2 DTA domestic lamp plants and 1 EOU export lamp plant in India plus Luxlite Luxembourg, and Global Cables & Mechatronics spanning Automotive (SAL) 1 EOU India, Non-Automotive 1 EOU India, Suprajit UK (including Suprajit Slovenia), Suprajit USA, Suprajit Hungary, Shanghai Lonestar China, Suprajit Canada, Suprajit Germany, Wescon-SENA (Suprajit Kansas), Suprajit Brownsville, Suprajit Matamoros, Suprajit Morocco and Suprajit Jiaxing China, alongside the Technology Center. On the energy side a 1811 KW solar plant was commissioned in Unit 5, Unit 7 and Unit 4, eliminating the need for installing higher-capacity generators, net metering agreements with TANGEDCO were completed, procurement of 5.89 million units of green energy annually through group captive power vendors was finalised and implemented for all Karnataka units as of March 2026 (with 1.2 MW under discussion for the PLE A-1 plants), and a VFD-based system installed in Units 5, 14, 12 and 16 will be extended to all other plants in a phased manner aligned with capacity expansion. Historically the group's footprint was built through seven acquisitions - five in cables and two in halogen bulbs - including Speedo Cable Business (PV) of Pricol, Phoenix Lamps Limited, Wescon Controls (Wichita, USA), CTP Gills Cables (now Suprajit Europe), Shah Concabs, the Osram Karnai plant (Phoenix Division) and the Cable Division (LDC) of Kongsberg Automotive, with new plants at SAL Bengaluru, Pathredi, Chennai, Sanand, Pantnagar, Haridwar and Manesar, a 100% EOU for non-automotive cables in Bengaluru, and the establishment of Suprajit Technology Centre, Suprajit Germany and Suprajit Canada.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leader in automotive cables in the world and third largest control cable manufacturer by volume, producing more than 300 million cables a year
- 'De-risk and Diversify' strategy: diverse presence across geographies, products, customers and segments leaves the Company better positioned than peers amid rising trade barriers and tariff actions
- 'On-Shore, Near-Shore and Off-Shore' plant positioning for the US and EU markets, increasingly valued by customers in the current tariff environment and fitting the global 'China + 1' trend
- Pole position in India for halogen lamps in both OEM and aftermarket, with worldwide export supplies; reducing halogen capacity elsewhere and the insolvency of a leading halogen manufacturer support a 'Last Man Standing' position
- Recognised by OEMs and Tier-1 players globally as a preferred cable and control system provider with a global R&D and manufacturing footprint
- Suprajit Technology Centre as the group's technology backbone, commercialising braking, actuator and electronics products, plus a technology tie-up with Blubrake for a low-cost ABS for the Indian market
- Added capability in braking systems and electronics/mechatronics enables a shift from component supplier to 'Technology and Solution provider' - the 'Beyond Cables' journey
- Long-standing trust of major automotive OEMs in Europe and the USA and their Tier-1 vendors
- Globally co-ordinated engineering effort led from India, leveraging deep cable knowledge across the group and time-zone advantage
- Operational recognition: JIPM Award for TPM Excellence at two cable units and ACMA recognition for operational excellence at national level in the Tier-1 community
- Group-wide standardisation through phased SAP roll-out and the 'One Suprajit Initiative' (SAP, PLM, IoT)
